clue.text: Traveller is second to be stopped by crowd

indicators.note: the word for second is blocked partway through by the crowd word, which sits inside it

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it, so a seconder is a backer
a pack is a crowd or mob

explanation.surface: A traveller supports a motion but gets hemmed in by the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack-carrying budget tourist is a typical kind of traveller.

clue.text: Help with answer moved to the start of round

indicators.note: the answer letter is shifted from inside the round word to its front

parts.note: a beat is a policeman's regular round

explanation.surface: Instructions for shuffling a letter in a puzzle round.
explanation.walkthrough: Shifting the A of BEAT to the front gives the four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist, usually in wrongdoing, a synonym of help.

clue.text: Squeezing teacher after vacation to fit into old suit

indicators.note: the emptied teacher goes inside the phrase for an old suit

parts.note: ex- means former, old
an action is a lawsuit

indicators.note: vacating a word empties out its middle, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A teacher back from holiday struggles to squeeze into an old suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after vacation' empties teacher to its outer letters; 'old suit' is a former lawsuit, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraction is drawing something out by pressure, as juice is squeezed out of fruit.

clue.text: Damaging allegations about a legislative assembly

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for allegations is read backwards

parts.note: mud is slander, as in mud-slinging

explanation.surface: A parliament is the subject of damaging allegations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the allegations word round. The Duma is Russia's parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duma is the elected legislative assembly of Russia.

clue.text: Controversial sequel involved cops in boat at sea

indicators.note: to cop is to catch or take, so the first jumble takes the second inside it
involved means tangled, so the letters of sequel are mixed up
at sea means confused, so the letters of in boat are scrambled

explanation.surface: A film sequel about police on a boat drew controversy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges SEQUEL to QUESLE, which 'cops' (catches) TIONAB, the jumble of IN BOAT that 'at sea' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Something questionable is open to doubt or dispute, hence controversial.

clue.text: Live tour band's leader somehow put together too elaborately

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together in some unstated order
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A band's live tour was assembled in an overblown manner.
explanation.walkthrough: LIVE TOUR plus B from band's are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A building that is overbuilt has been constructed with more elaboration than needed.

clue.text: Group first to object about tweet oddly

indicators.note: the first letter of object is taken

parts.note: C, for circa, is Latin for about

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd positions of tweet

explanation.surface: A group is the first to object to an odd tweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes T, E, T from tweet.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight, especially musicians.

clue.text: One group of workers is mostly untrustworthy

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: shifty means evasive and untrustworthy

explanation.surface: A group of workers is said to be mostly dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of SHIFTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a team of employees working a set period, such as the night crew.

clue.text: Apparent worth of clock, posh, received in farewell

parts.note: a clock face is the dial; clock can stand for face by association

indicators.note: the posh letter is taken inside the farewell word

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: A posh clock is handed over as a leaving present.
explanation.definitionFit: The face value of something is its apparent worth on the surface, as opposed to its real worth.

clue.text: Force, it's said, with batting, mostly successful?

indicators.note: it's said means the word for force is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to prise open is to force open

indicators.note: mostly removes the final letter of the batting word

parts.note: an innings is a team's or player's turn at batting in cricket

explanation.surface: A forceful batting display that was largely a success.
explanation.walkthrough: PRISE sounds like PRIZE; INNINGS (a turn batting in cricket) loses its S. The question mark marks the definition as loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A prizewinning entry has won a prize, so it is successful in a competition.

clue.text: Indian prince beheaded by Greek hero

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is removed from the prince

parts.note: a raja is an Indian prince
X is the multiplication sign, as in 3 by 4

explanation.surface: An Indian prince is beheaded by a Greek hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' strips R from RAJA; X stands for 'by', as in 3x4.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax was a mighty warrior on the Greek side in the Trojan War.

clue.text: Have desired result poor mothers like for pound less

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the letters are reassembled
less means taken away, removing the pound letter from like

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Poor mothers make do with less than a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes L from LIKE, leaving IKE; 'poor' rearranges MOTHERS plus IKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow that strikes home hits its target, so the phrase means achieving the intended effect.

clue.text: Row supporter's ending after match

indicators.note: after places the supporter's final letter behind the match word

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A row breaks out among supporters at the end of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one row of seating in a series rising above another.

clue.text: Promoter opposing resistance, overcoming this regularly

indicators.note: overcoming here means sitting over, enclosing the regular letters

parts.note: adverse means opposing, hostile

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of this

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A promoter overcomes opposition and resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes alternate letters of 'this'; 'overcoming' has the outer pieces sit over them.
explanation.definitionFit: An advertiser promotes goods or services publicly.

clue.text: Raised funds on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means as heard, so the funds word is taken by its sound

parts.note: bread is slang for money, funds

explanation.surface: Money was raised through a radio appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bred is to have been brought up, raised.

clue.text: Name revolutionary European movement out of control

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Naming a revolutionary European movement that ran out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: E + TIC read backwards gives the four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite someone is to name them, as in court or as a source.

clue.text: A bar eccentric chap carries after exercise for food

indicators.note: after puts the exercise letters before the rest

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise

indicators.note: carries means the eccentric chap holds the bar word inside

parts.note: a nutter is a crazy person
but means except, as does bar

explanation.surface: An odd fellow takes a bar along after his workout to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' is the preposition meaning except, not a snack bar; 'carries' puts it inside the eccentric chap.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread made from ground roasted nuts is a common food.

clue.text: Attractive people needing close to impeccable skin

indicators.note: needing here means lacking, so a letter goes missing

parts.note: cuties are attractive people

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Attractive people need impeccable skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' means wanting, i.e. lacking: E, the close of impeccable, is dropped from CUTIES.
explanation.definitionFit: The cutis is the anatomical term for the skin, the dermis and epidermis.

clue.text: In cities all over the place became bigheaded

indicators.note: In tells us the became word goes inside the jumbled cities
all over the place means scattered, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: got means became, as in got angry

explanation.surface: Someone became conceited while travelling to cities everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' gives EISTIC from cities; 'In' puts the became word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being egotistic means conceited and self-absorbed, hence bigheaded.

clue.text: Policeman once with low confidence

parts.note: blue means depressed, low in spirits
bottle is British slang for nerve or confidence

explanation.surface: A former policeman lacking confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: BOTTLE is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebottle was old slang for a police officer, from the blue uniform.

clue.text: Hears about two different short ways to produce parodies

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the court word goes around the ways

parts.note: a judge tries or hears a case
Ave and St are abbreviations for avenue and street
Ave and St are abbreviations for avenue and street

explanation.surface: Hearings about two shortcuts produced farces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hears' is what a judge does to a case; 'about' wraps it round the two road abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Travesties are absurd or grotesque imitations, mocking versions of the real thing.

clue.text: Unsuitable home, sister's place, that is new inside

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: inside places the following letters within the sister's place

parts.note: a convent is where a nun, a sister, lives
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A home in a convent is unsuitable, being new.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inconvenient is ill-suited or awkward for one's needs.

clue.text: Extremely hesitant about flower arrangement? Aspidistra for one

indicators.note: about means around, so the extremes of hesitant enclose the rest
extremely picks the outermost letters of hesitant

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Ouse
a plan is an arrangement

explanation.surface: Unsure about arranging flowers, one settles for an aspidistra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river (something that flows): the OUSE, a river in England. 'Extremely' gives H and T to surround OUSE + PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a classic hardy indoor plant, an example of a potted indoor plant.

clue.text: Split with current partner is fair

parts.note: to leg it is to run away, to split
I is the symbol for electric current
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: Splitting up with your current partner is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Legitimate means lawful or justifiable, hence fair.

clue.text: Imposed large deficit possibly involving negotiations at the outset

indicators.note: involving means taking in the first letter of negotiations
possibly suggests one possible rearrangement of the letters
at the outset takes the first letter

explanation.surface: A large deficit was imposed after negotiations began.
explanation.walkthrough: L + DEFICIT is rearranged to IFLICTED, with N, the first letter of negotiations, inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To have inflicted something is to have forced it on someone.

clue.text: I will interrupt snitch half way through commotion

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break in, so the letter goes inside
half way through places it at the middle of the snitch word

parts.note: a nose is slang for an informer, a snitch

explanation.surface: Someone vows to cut short a snitch midway through an uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snitch' is a slang noun for an informer; 'half way through' places I at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is loud disturbing sound, a din or commotion.

clue.text: Greet upwardly mobile southern person in charge

indicators.note: in a down clue moving upward reverses the word for greet

parts.note: to greet is an old and Scots word meaning to weep, sob

explanation.surface: An upwardly mobile southerner greets the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greet' is the Scots word for weep, not welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is the one in charge of others at work.

clue.text: Assume energy is required in battle

indicators.note: is required in puts the energy letter within the battle word

parts.note: war is a battle on a large scale
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Energy is needed to fight a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear an expression is to adopt or assume it.
